thesis_statement: Netflix remains the scaled streaming category leader converting pricing power, ads and membership growth into 13% revenue growth at a 33% operating margin - with a Q2'26 caveat: engagement growth slowed to +2% view hours and the stock sits below its SQL band low, so the market is already pricing a growth-quality question the second half must answer.

base.summary: Revenue grows 13-14% through 2026 ($51.0-51.4B) with a ~31.5% operating margin, as price changes land as expected and content amortization growth slows in H2.
drivers: ads revenue growing with enhanced AI-driven capabilities

bull.summary: Engagement accelerates back above the +1.5% 2025 pace as the H1 sports-schedule drag (Olympics, World Cup) fades, live events and games expand variety, and the model re-rates on sustained double-digit growth with margin expansion.
drivers: view hours +2% in H1 despite Olympics/World Cup competition
price changes performing in line across regions
content slate breadth (series, films, video podcasts, creator content, cloud TV games)

bear.summary: Engagement growth decelerates further as competition and content saturation bite, pricing power exhausts, and the market de-rates the multiple on single-digit growth - with the current below-band price showing that repricing has already started.
drivers: view-hour growth only +2% vs revenue +13% (price-led growth)
UCAN price change only partial-quarter in Q2

key_risks: Growth is increasingly price-led, not engagement-led: revenue +13% against view hours +2%. If engagement stalls, the pricing lever has a ceiling.

The close (71.14 on 09-25) sits inside the SQL band (70.11-75.54) but at the low end, 1.5% above the invalidation level (66.84) - the market is already leaning on the growth-quality question. The stale SQL BELOW_STOP label (08-21 snapshot) is one of the five known-wrong labels and disagrees with the live in-band position.
Content amortization grows faster than revenue in H1; the H2 slowdown to ~10% is guidance, not yet fact.
Ads business scale is still small relative to the core; monetization improvements are expected, not proven.

invalidation_reasons.price: Close below the live guarded-SQL reference_invalidation_level (66.84 at the 2026-09-26 renewal). SQL governs after any later renewal; this text does not.
fundamental: Revenue growth falls below 8% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
View-hour growth turns negative year over year for two consecutive quarters.

catalysts.event: Engagement trajectory after the Olympics/World Cup H1 drag

evidence.claim: Q2 2026: revenue $12.6B +13% (+12% FX-neutral); operating income $4.2B +11%; operating margin 33.4% vs 34.1%; diluted EPS $0.80 +11%; FCF $1.5B; view hours +2% H1 vs +1.5% in 2025 despite Olympics/World Cup competition; price changes consistent with expectations (UCAN partial-quarter); 2026 outlook narrowed to $51.0-51.4B revenue (13-14% growth) at 31.5% operating margin; Q3 forecast $12.86B revenue +12%, 33.2% margin; EMEA passed $4.0B quarterly revenue; content amortization to grow ~10% for 2026 (H2-weighted)
evidence.source: Netflix Q2 2026 Letter to Shareholders, SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1 (sec.gov .../ex991_q226.htm, 2026-07-16)

evidence.claim: Aggregator row current at Q2 2026 (period_end 2026-06-30, data_quality clean); trailing P/E 22.37, forward P/E 18.66, P/B 9.83, net debt $5.21B

SQL band 70.11-75.54, invalidation 66.84, reference_confidence 40; close 71.14 on 2026-09-25 is inside band, near the low end; the stale SQL BELOW_STOP label (08-21 snapshot) is a known-wrong label and disagrees with the live position
